ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all directors, shareholders, and UBOs against OFAC SDN List, UN Consolidated List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, and Canadian sanctions schedules under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act (Magnitsky), and the Regulations Implementing the United Nations Resolutions; mandatory PEP (politically exposed person) assessment per FINTRAC guidance, including family members and close associates, with enhanced due diligence for foreign PEPs; records of screening and CDD to be retained for at least five years under PCMLTFA Part 1.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: BC Corporate Online Registry (corporateonline.gov.bc.ca) and BC Registries NUANS-integrated corporate name search via authorized service providers
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must be in English or French with English transliteration for non-Roman scripts; the name must comprise a distinctive element, a descriptive element (optional), and the legal element 'Unlimited Liability Company' or 'ULC'; names must not be identical or confusingly similar to registered or reserved names per BCA ss.21-25 and Name Regulation.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name refusal under BCA s.24(5), the applicant may submit written submissions, a revised name, and a fresh NUANS report (maximum 90 days old) to the BC Registrar of Companies within 21 days of refusal for reconsideration; if refusal is upheld, the applicant may seek judicial review in the Supreme Court of British Columbia under the Judicial Review Procedure Act, R.S.B.C. 1996, c.241; a new reservation or an extension of an existing reservation may also be requested before expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for the statutory registered office only where a licensed BC registered agent or corporate services provider supplies a physical BC street address for service and records inspection; operational tax substance cannot be satisfied by a virtual office alone, and a Canadian permanent establishment may be found where the ULC has employees or a functional head office in Canada.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low (approximately 5% annual likelihood) for a digital-only video matching platform without a money services business (MSB) licence; increasing to moderate-to-high if the entity acts as an MSB or processes Paymentwall/Apple IAP funds, because FINTRAC may conduct examinations and BC/Canada tax authorities may conduct unannounced audit visits under audit warrants.

The registered office of the Company is established at [full street address, city, province, postal code in British Columbia]. The initial directors of the Company are appointed as [full names and addresses of at least one director]. The officers of the Company are appointed as President [name], Secretary [name], and such other officers as may be necessary. All actions of the incorporator in preparing the Articles of Incorporation are ratified and confirmed. This resolution is passed this [date] day of [month], [year].

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) / Agence du revenu du Canada (ARC) — federal authority for the Business Number (BN), GST/HST (Part IX of the Excise Tax Act), and Part I corporate income tax; online portals: Business Registration Online (BRO), CRA My Business Account, and GST/HST NETFILE (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency.html). Provincial component: British Columbia Ministry of Finance, Consumer Taxation Branch (BC PST administration) and BC Registry Services (corporate registry for the ULC).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a British Columbia Unlimited Liability Corporation (BC ULC): (1) incorporate under the British Columbia Business Corporations Act via BC Corporate Online/OneStop Business Registry to obtain the BC incorporation number; (2) register with the CRA for the nine-digit Business Number (BN) and program accounts — RT (GST/HST), RC (federal corporate income tax), and RM (import/export, if applicable) — through BRO or Form RC1; GST/HST registration becomes mandatory when taxable supplies made in Canada exceed C$30,000 in a single calendar quarter or over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters under ETA ss. 148-149, and may be elected earlier to recover input tax credits; (3) where the ULC is owned by a non-resident parent, the ULC itself is the Canadian resident registrant and no separate non-resident registration is required; if the platform were instead operated by a non-resident entity without Canadian incorporation, registration under the CRA non-resident digital-economy GST/HST regime would apply; (4) register separately with the BC Consumer Taxation Branch (Form FIN 418) for BC Provincial Sales Tax (PST) if the ULC makes taxable PST supplies such as telecommunication services; (5) retain the BN confirmation and GST/HST registration certificate in CRA My Business Account as proof of identity for cross-border counterparties and zero-rating substantiation.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Canadian statutory default) with Pass_Through_Eligible attributes for foreign members. Under the Income Tax Act (Canada), the BC ULC is a corporation (ITA s. 248(1)), a resident taxable Canadian corporation subject to Part I entity-level tax: federal 15% general rate (9% small-business rate) combined with British Columbia 12% general rate (9% small-business rate on active business income up to C$500,000, subject to associated-corporation rules), filing Form T2. Canada does not permit a domestic check-the-box or partnership election for the ULC; however, for U.S. federal income tax purposes the ULC is an eligible entity under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3, so a single-member ULC may be disregarded and a multi-member ULC may be taxed as a partnership (Form 8832), with Canadian income flowing through to U.S. members subject to the fiscally-transparent tie-breaker in Article IV(6) of the Canada-U.S. Income Tax Convention and to the Canadian hybrid-mismatch rules enacted under the 2021 federal budget. For GST/HST, the ULC is a distinct person from its shareholders and all supplies are reported by the ULC.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: (1) U.S. check-the-box election: filing IRS Form 8832 under Treas. Reg. § 301.7701-3 to classify the BC ULC as a partnership (multi-member) or disregarded entity (single-member) for U.S. federal income tax purposes, with no Canadian domestic equivalent — the ULC remains a corporation under the Income Tax Act; (2) treaty-based flow-through relief: CRA administrative recognition of U.S. members' treaty claims where the ULC is fiscally transparent under Article IV(6) of the Canada-U.S. Convention, subject to the hybrid-mismatch limitation rules; (3) GST/HST elections: early small-supplier registration, quarterly or annual filing frequency under ETA s. 238(1), the Quick Method of accounting (CRA Form GST74) for qualifying registrants with annual taxable revenues not exceeding C$400,000, and appointment of a Canadian representative under ETA s. 267.1 for non-resident registrants or refund claimants; (4) the ITA s. 216 election for non-residents deriving Canadian rental/timber income is not applicable to this operating software business; (5) no Canadian statutory mechanism exists to elect partnership treatment for a ULC, and CRA may recharacterize artificial structures designed to produce hybrid deductions.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada) as the sole central bank; Canada maintains a fully liberalized FX regime with no separate Foreign Exchange Administration. Currency controls are exercised solely through ongoing payment system oversight and monetary policy.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible on both current and capital accounts. No restrictions on cross-border capital movements, dividend/distribution remittances, or profit repatriation. Remittances are subject to Canadian tax withholding and enhanced AML screening, but there is no commercial convertibility approval requirement. The Bank of Canada does not require licences for FX dealing by corporates.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory export proceeds surrender requirements or mandatory conversion ratios exist in Canada. All export receipts may be retained in CAD or any freely convertible currency, provided they conform to anti-money laundering / FINTRAC reporting thresholds (e.g., large cash transaction reports, cross-border currency movement reporting).

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Trade Finance / Commercial Letter of Credit

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium — Strictly constrained. Domestic digital payment service providers (e.g., Wise, Payoneer, Revolut) may be engaged as payment facilitators, but they must be registered as money service businesses (MSB) with FINTRAC. A BC ULC may use these to obtain virtual/FX accounts, but only for non-deposit-taking payment activity; the EMI cannot legally venture into Canadian deposit-taking functions unless chartered under the Bank Act. Cross-border offshore EMIs require Canadian registration to clear CAD wires; otherwise settlement shifts to US-dollar omnibus accounts and onward SWIFT settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally mandatory for a BC-incorporated ULC applying for a commercial banking account, unless the relationship manager permits a remote video-conferenced interview under Bank Act anti-money-laundering directives (FINTRAC). Directors with 25%+ control residue must be verified. Remote opening remains possible only when the ULC maintains a substantive Canadian nexus (registered office in BC, Canadian resident corporate officer or designated signatory with authority over accounts). For non-resident ULC directors, a notarized/legalized passport and source-of-funds evidence are compulsory; absence of a physical interview escalates the bank to Enhanced Due Diligence and may take 7–15 business days.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident directors and foreign ultimate beneficial owners with a pass-through ULC structure
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: BC Corporate Registry Company Summary; constitutional documents (Articles/Notice of Articles); registered office address; notarized passports of all shareholders and directors; CFTA ultimate beneficial ownership declaration; audited source-of-funds statements; independent legal opinion confirming the ULC's tax classification and unlimited liability characteristics.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Video-chat social app generating frequent small-value global payments
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Third-party AML audit report; transaction flow diagrams; chargeback and fraud prevention policy; PCI DSS compliance certificate; app store merchant agreements; data mapping under PIPEDA; operational incident-response procedures; evidence of real-time age-verification and geolocation tracking.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of offshore digital EMIs and alternative payment rails (Apple IAP, Paymentwall)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Payment processor ISO/IEC 27001 certification; FINTRAC MSB registration certificate of the EMI; processor's AML/CFT program summary; contractual flow demonstrating independent end-user KYC; evidence that the EMI's license/registration status is current in its home jurisdiction; consolidated settlement statements showing segregated funds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Anonymous in-app gifting and crypto-asset proceeds as source of liquidity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IP and device fingerprinting policy; digital identity verification procedures under the Bank Act; balanced mix of documented bank statements and audited financials; transaction monitoring policy with AI/ML alert thresholds; clear banning and reporting tools for anonymous users; evidence of compliance with the Financial Consumer Agency of Canada and OSFI disclosure standards.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Standard inbound equity/debt remittances to a BC ULC clear through SWIFT MT103 with a supplementary payment message. Wires should reference: (a) remittance purpose code 'G210' (personal/company investment) or the Bank of Canada-side trial code; (b) beneficiary BC ULC name and account number; (c) the SWIFT BIC of the correspondent. Domestic CAD transfers settle over Payments Canada Lynx (large-value transfer system). For non-CAD capital, settle in USD over US Fedwire/CHIPS, convert at spot to CAD, or hold USD in a cross-border DDA. Verification: source-of-funds disclosure, entity resolution, AML block screen, and UBO declaration for filings under the BC Business Corporations Act.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for high-value subscriptions will flow via SWIFT MT103 (customer credit transfer) or an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (LC) where the supplier demands a documentary undertaking. The ULC's bank will require credit approval for the LC; then the bank issues the LC in favour of the vendor with a fixed USD number. For recurring small-ticket app disbursements, clearing uses automated clearing (Payments Canada ACSS), or international USD zero-balance accounts at a US clearing bank. All payments are subject to FINTRAC large-value reporting (CAD 10,000+), Canadian sanctions screening (Canadian Regulations SOR/2023), and OFAC rules if USD settlement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) — permissible only while underlying transaction is not settled in CAD; rarely needed for Canadian source FX
Cross-Currency Swaps (EUR/USD and CAD/USD) for term financing
European-Style FX Options for defined contractual exposures
Commodity or interest-rate swaps — not permissible under treasury policy

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: British Columbia Registrar of Companies (BC Corporate Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within two months after the anniversary date of incorporation or of the last annual report, whichever is later
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty; failure to file for two consecutive years may result in administrative strike-off and dissolution, requiring formal restoration proceedings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within six months after each taxation year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalty of 5% of unpaid balance plus 1% per full month up to 12 months, daily penalty when no tax is payable, compound statutory interest, and possible criminal prosecution for repeat failure

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Not triggered by revenue or asset size; audit appointment may be waived by unanimous shareholder consent for non-reporting companies. Mandatory for reporting issuers and for companies subject to specific statutory audit requirements.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian GAAP: IFRS (Part I of CPA Canada Handbook) for reporting issuers; Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE, Part II) for eligible private companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Share transfers must be recorded in the register of members; if the company is subject to significant-control transparency reporting, changes must be updated within 30 days. The annual report filing serves as the annual confirmation that the company's registers and beneficial-ownership records are accurate.
